titleEn: Klīṃ is Kṛṣṇa. The seed of longing — the pull of the flute.
meaningEn: Klīṃ is the seed of longing — the Tantras' kāma-bīja, the seed of desire and of being drawn. In the Navārṇa it is the third seed, aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ, where the ritual frame calls it the kīlaka — the peg that fastens the mantra — and modern teachers read it as Mahākālī, the Mother's pull. It belongs to Kṛṣṇa: his eighteen-syllable mantra in the Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad opens klīṃ kṛṣṇāya govindāya…, and it is Kāmadeva's seed too.
meaningHi: क्लीं चाह का बीज है — तंत्र इसे काम-बीज कहते हैं, चाह का और खिंचे चले आने का बीज। नवार्ण में यह तीसरा बीज है, ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं, जहाँ पाठ-विधि इसे कीलक कहती है — मंत्र को बाँधने वाली खूँटी — और आज के जानकार इसे महाकाली पढ़ते हैं, माँ का खिंचाव। यह कृष्ण का है: गोपाल-तापनी उपनिषद में उनका अठारह अक्षर का मंत्र क्लीं कृष्णाय गोविन्दाय… से शुरू होता है, और यह कामदेव का बीज भी है।
sayItLike: kleem — 'k' + 'l' run together, long 'ee', then a hum

words.glossEn: Kāma — and Kṛṣṇa — in the Tantras' reading
words.glossHi: काम — और कृष्ण — तंत्र के हिसाब से
words.grammar: Varada Tantra kośa via Woodroffe: ka = Kāmadeva / Kṛṣṇa

words.glossEn: Indra — lordship, in the same reading
contentment — tuṣṭi, in the same reading
the dot (ं) — the closing hum, bindu and nāda
words.glossHi: बिंदी (ं) — अंत की गूँज, बिन्दु और नाद
words.grammar: kośa: 'the giver of joy' — tradition's attribution, not a meaning

source.text: Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad (Kṛṣṇa's eighteen-syllable mantra); Śāradā-tilaka Tantra (11th c.); Varada Tantra as quoted in Woodroffe, Garland of Letters (1922)
source.ref: the kāma-bīja; opens klīṃ kṛṣṇāya govindāya gopījanavallabhāya svāhā; third seed of the Navārṇa, where the Saptaśatī vidhi names it 'klīṃ kīlakam'
source.note: The Gopāla-tāpanī is a late Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad. The letter reading is the Tantras' kośa method, not etymology. 'Klīṃ = Mahākālī' inside the Navārṇa is modern commentary (Satyananda Saraswati; Devadatta Kali, 2003), not the vidhi's wording.

significance.textSays: Gopāla-tāpanī: Kṛṣṇa's mantra begins klīṃ. The Saptaśatī vidhi: 'klīṃ kīlakam' — klīṃ is the Navārṇa's peg. The Varada Tantra's kośa reads ka as Kāma, la as Indra, ī as contentment.
significance.traditionSays: Kṛṣṇa's and Kāmadeva's seed — the sound of being drawn, the way the gopīs were drawn by the flute; middle of the Bālā triad aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ; read by modern teachers as Mahākālī within the Navārṇa.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That it attracts a person, a partner or wealth. It names a pull toward the Lord; what is given is his.
